checks.s: The memo identifies the one-time easement payment (per-rod rate) in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding the company's delegated fallback negotiation authority.
The memo identifies the crop-loss and damages payment provisions (administrative surcharge and/or per-occurrence cap) in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding fallback authority.
The memo identifies the restoration standard (including timeline and/or performance metric) in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding fallback authority.
The memo identifies the indemnification scope (breadth of coverage and/or cap) in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding fallback authority.
The memo identifies the assignment and/or change-of-control consent requirement in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding fallback authority.
The memo identifies the term/reversionary interest provision (non-use reversion) in the Drennan counter-draft as exceeding fallback authority.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix maximum for the one-time easement payment is $12,500 per rod of centerline length.
The memo states that the Drennan Trust counter-proposal sets the one-time easement payment at $16,750 per rod of centerline length.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix authorizes a crop-loss administrative surcharge of 15% of actual documented loss.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix includes a per-occurrence cap of $275,000 on crop-loss and damages payments.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal increases the crop-loss administrative surcharge to 30% of actual documented loss.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal removes or eliminates the per-occurrence cap on crop-loss and damages payments (i.e., no cap).
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix requires restoration to 'substantially similar' pre-construction condition, or words to that effect.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix requires restoration within 18 months of construction completion.

The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal requires restoration to 'original agricultural productivity' measured by the three-year pre-construction average yield per acre and/or certified by a mutually agreed independent agronomist.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal shortens the restoration timeline to 12 months from the fallback's 18 months.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal includes liquidated damages of $1,500 per acre per month triggered by failure to meet the restoration standard or timeline.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix limits Meridian's indemnity obligation to third-party claims arising from Meridian's negligence or willful misconduct.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix sets an aggregate indemnification liability cap equal to 200% of the one-time easement payment.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal imposes a broad-form indemnity covering all claims 'arising out of or related to' the easement, including the Grantor's own concurrent negligence.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal eliminates or removes the aggregate cap on indemnification liability (i.e., no aggregate cap).
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix permits Meridian to freely assign the easement to any affiliate or project lender without grantor consent.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix requires only 30 days' prior written notice for assignment to an unaffiliated third party, with no grantor consent right.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal requires the Grantor's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, for any assignment or change of control, whether direct or indirect.
The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal imposes a $50,000 'transfer processing fee' upon any assignment or change of control.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix provides for a perpetual easement that can be extinguished only by a recorded release (i.e., no reversion trigger).

The memo states that the Drennan counter-proposal includes automatic reversion of the easement to the Grantor if the easement is not used for its stated utility purpose for any continuous 24-month period.
The memo references July 15, 2025 as the deadline by which all interconnection-route easements must be fully executed.
The memo identifies the July 15, 2025 easement execution deadline as a requirement of the project-finance term sheet with Great Plains Infrastructure Lenders, LP (GPIL).
The memo states that the easement corridor across the Drennan Trust parcel is the only technically and environmentally viable interconnection route for the Tallgrass Solar Project.
The memo states that rerouting around the Drennan parcel would require a new environmental review estimated at 9 to 14 months.
The memo is addressed, directed, or sent to the Meridian Prairie Energy LLC Investment Committee (IC) and/or its chair, CFO Dana Okonkwo.
The memo identifies Nathan Xu (Senior Counsel – Project Development, Meridian) as its author or sender.
The memo specifically references the Fallback Authority Matrix by version number, v.4.1.
The memo references March 3, 2025 as the approval date of the Fallback Authority Matrix by the Investment Committee.
The memo uses an approximate corridor length of 2.1 miles and/or approximately 672 rods when calculating the incremental one-time easement payment exposure.
The memo identifies or uses the per-rod price differential of approximately $4,250 ($16,750 counter-proposal minus $12,500 fallback maximum) when calculating the incremental exposure.
The memo states that the approximate aggregate incremental one-time easement payment exposure above fallback authority is approximately $2.85 million, or roughly $2.8M to $2.9M.

The memo flags that the Drennan counter-proposal's assignment/change-of-control consent requirement could impede Meridian's ability to assign or pledge the easement to its project-finance lender, Great Plains Infrastructure Lenders, LP (GPIL), and notes that the fallback authority contemplates free assignment to project lenders.

The memo makes a clear, specific request to the Meridian Investment Committee to authorize negotiation authority beyond the Fallback Authority Matrix for the identified out-of-policy terms on the Drennan Trust easement.
